scenes.text: 古代的时候有一个人叫神农。他需要当上医，一看别的人就想帮助他们。但是，他有一个问题，他不知道什么东西能做药。神农听说一个远远的地方有一种植物，什么病人吃都会觉得身体更好。神农三个月走去，找到有植物的地方，他看到一个很漂亮的植物，又香又好看。

## Relevant grammar rule cards (ground your explanations in these)

### Rule: ambiguous_reference
Grammar/linguistic point: ambiguous_reference
Ambiguous or vague referent (pronoun 他/她 unclear, vague noun like 人/事情/别人 needing specificity).
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 妈妈老是工作了，害得她的身体不好 -> 孟母  [“妈妈” here is ambiguous; 老是工作，no了for routine/habit]
  - 夹竹桃一吃，就生病了 -> 他就生病了  [otherwise it is ambiguous who gets sick]
  - 他送三个梨给他们 -> 送了  [了completed; “他” is a bit ambiguous]
  - 人一直在墓地大声哭 -> 来祭拜的人  [“人“ is too general and too vague, and does not stand alone]
  - 他一吃黄色的花就有麻烦 -> 肚子就疼  [“有麻烦“ is too vague]
  - 他停在树下 -> here “他” is a bit ambiguous, it can refer to the boy or the man wearing the scarf.
  - 古代的时候，有一个妈妈和他的儿子，这个小孩子叫孟子 -> 在古代，“她”，有一个妈妈和她的儿子住在一起，儿子叫孟子  [“这个小孩子” is unclear and ambiguous]
  - 因为他想知道什么植物能吃，他看到什么植物就吃什么 -> 因为神农想知道……，所以……  [the first他is a bit ambiguous]

### Rule: character_introduction_first_mention
Grammar/linguistic point: character_introduction_first_mention
A character should be briefly introduced on first mention (name + who they are) rather than assumed known.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 古代的时候，孟子和孟母住在一起 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 为了帮人们找到他们的饭，神农开始找我们可以吃的植物 -> 找到可以吃的植物  [delete我们；better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 就看到很漂亮的女孩 -> 一个很漂亮的女孩  [first appearing noun should not be specific]
  - 在古代时候，孟子跟他妈妈常常搬家 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 这是一个神农的古代故事 -> 关于神农的  [better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 古代的时候，孟子和他的妈妈住在离墓地很近 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears；住在离墓地很近的地方，住在+Place]
  - 神农和他的城市不知道什么植物他们可以吃 -> 人们不知道什么植物可以吃  [delete他们；better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears]
  - 古代的时候，一个家人住在中国。那个家人是孟子的家人 -> 在古代，孟子一家人住在中国  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]

### Rule: time_expression
Grammar/linguistic point: time_expression
Time expressions: 在古代 (not 古代的时候), 后来 vs. 以后 vs. 将来, 长大以后, Time + 以后; 'then' in a narrative is 然后/后来, not 以后 alone.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 古代的时候，孟子和孟母住在一起 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 很多年的时候，他测试别的植物 -> 他尝试各种植物尝试了很多年  [“别的” is for “a different type”, and “all else except the spoken one”]
  - 秋季期间 not very natural -> 整个秋季期间；Time + 期间：usually special, long period, “秋季” itself is not “special” enough, “整个/今年秋季” would highlight this particular, special period.
  - 在古代时候，孟子跟他妈妈常常搬家 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 他以后正好看一个灵芝，他一吃灵芝就身体好了 -> 然后  [Time+以后；他正好看到，看look vs.看到see; 身体就好了，Subj. + 就]
  - 古代的时候，孟子和他的妈妈住在离墓地很近 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears；住在离墓地很近的地方，住在+Place]
  - 以后他知道灵芝没有毒，夹竹桃有毒，它可以做药 -> 后来  [Time+以后；“它“ is unclear, it seems that it refers to夹竹桃，which is a poison, not a medicine]
  - 古代的时候，一个家人住在中国。那个家人是孟子的家人 -> 在古代，孟子一家人住在中国  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]

### Rule: redundancy_delete
Grammar/linguistic point: redundancy_delete
Redundant word/phrase that should simply be deleted (repeated subject, repeated adverb, etc.).
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 孟母找到了良好的工作，她挣不少钱 -> 好工作  [良好is not with工作；delete她, redundant]
  - 神农出发在一个旅程，他在这个旅程尝了很多植物 -> 神农开始了旅程，在旅程中  [delete他，redundant]
  - 一个农人爬着一个树，他把树上的梨子摘下来 -> 农民；一棵树；delete他，otherwise redundant.
  - 第一次他们搬家，他们在墓地住 -> 他们第一次搬家是在墓地住  [delete the second他们，redundant]
  - 神农回他的家，他看到了药，正好看到了毒植物 -> 回到家  [delete他的, redundant; delete他，redundant; 有毒植物；what is the connection between 看到了药and正好看到了有毒植物?]
  - 这个坏人好像没有什么有希望的前途 -> 没有什么前途；“前途” itself means “hopeful future”, so “有希望” is a little bit redundant.
  - 他写太多的文章，他建议孩子们常常做祭拜 -> 写了  [了completed; delete the second他, redundant; 祭拜]
  - 神农看他的朋友很生病，他想帮他们，所以神农去了大山 -> 病得很重  [“生病” is not an Adj., so it cannot be with 很 or 不; delete the second他and the second神农，redundant]

## Nearby real correction exemplars (style reference for how to phrase corrections)

- 所以神农走了很长的时间找到植物药：能做药的植物

- 神农想帮大家找到好吃的菜：植物，better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears

- 神农看到人一吃百草就生病：better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears；人们，一些植物，“百草“ is a general term for “different plants”

## Student's scene to review
古代的时候有一个人叫神农。他需要当上医，一看别的人就想帮助他们。但是，他有一个问题，他不知道什么东西能做药。神农听说一个远远的地方有一种植物，什么病人吃都会觉得身体更好。神农三个月走去，找到有植物的地方，他看到一个很漂亮的植物，又香又好看。

scenes.feedback:
**Grammar Corrections**

Incorrect phrase: “古代的时候有一个人叫神农” / Formula: 在 + historical time + ，+ introduce character (name + role) / Correct: “在古代，有一个人叫神农。”  
“在古代” is more natural than “古代的时候.” You could also introduce him more clearly: “在古代，有一位想成为医生的人，叫神农。”

Incorrect phrase: “他需要当上医” / Formula: 谁 + 想/希望 + 成为 + 职业 / Correct: “他想成为一名医生。”  
“当上” usually emphasizes successfully obtaining a position, while “想成为” fits a personal goal better. “医” should be “医生” in modern Chinese.

Incorrect phrase: “一看别的人就想帮助他们” / Formula: 谁 + 一看到 + 人 + 就 + 想 + 帮助 + 他们 / Correct: “他一看到别人就想帮助他们。”  
Use “一看到” to mean “as soon as he sees.” “别人” is more natural than “别的人” here.

Incorrect phrase: “神农听说一个远远的地方有一种植物” / Formula: 听说 + 在 + place + 有 + noun / Correct: “神农听说在一个很远的地方有一种植物。”  
The place needs “在” before it. “远远的地方” can be replaced with the more natural “很远的地方.”

Incorrect phrase: “什么病人吃都会觉得身体更好” / Formula: 无论/任何 + noun + 吃了 + it + 都会 + result / Correct: “任何病人吃了它以后，身体都会好起来。”  
“什么病人” is not natural here. Also, use “它” to clearly refer to the plant.

Incorrect phrase: “神农三个月走去，找到有植物的地方” / Formula: 谁 + 走了/花了 + duration + ，才 + 找到 + place / Correct: “神农走了三个月，才找到了那种植物生长的地方。”  
“走了三个月” shows the completed duration, and “才” emphasizes that it took a long time. “有植物的地方” is too vague because many places have plants.

Incorrect phrase: “一个很漂亮的植物” / Formula: 一 + classifier + adjective + noun / Correct: “一种很美丽的植物。”  
The classifier for plants is usually “种,” not “个.”

**Vocabulary Suggestions**

Word: “帮助” / Context: “他一看到别人就想帮助他们。” / Alternatives: “救治” means to treat and save sick or injured people, so it fits especially well because Shennong wants to become a doctor. “帮助” is a general word for helping someone in any situation.

Word: “什么东西” / Context: “他不知道什么东西能做药。” / Alternatives: “什么植物” is more precise because the story is about medicinal plants. “药材” means medicinal materials or herbs and sounds more advanced; it is especially appropriate for traditional Chinese medicine.

Word: “远远的地方” / Context: “一个远远的地方” / Alternatives: “遥远的地方” is more natural and literary, often used in stories to describe a place far away. “很远的地方” is simpler and more conversational.

Word: “漂亮” / Context: “一个很漂亮的植物” / Alternatives: “美丽” is more suitable for flowers or plants and has a more elegant, descriptive feeling. “艳丽” emphasizes bright, striking colors, especially for flowers. “漂亮” is common but is used more often for people, clothes, or general appearance.

Word: “好看” / Context: “又香又好看” / Alternatives: “美观” means visually pleasing but is more formal. “赏心悦目” means so beautiful that it pleases the eyes; it is more advanced and literary. “好看” is simple and natural, but it is less vivid in a story.

**Encouragement and Next Steps**

You created a clear story sequence—from Shennong’s goal, to his problem, to his journey—and your description “又香又好看” makes the plant easy to imagine.  
Next time, focus on using precise classifiers and structures for duration, such as “走了三个月，才……”.

### Rule: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
Grammar/linguistic point: zhe_jiu_yao_kan
这就要看……了 ('it depends on ...') gives a flexible response to a question or uncertain condition instead of a direct answer. The part after 看 must be a question form: A-not-A (吃不吃), a wh-word, or A还是B.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 这个植物你能吃吗，这就要看植物的大小、植物的长短、植物的颜色了 -> 能不能吃  [delete the last two植物的]
  - 他们常常生病了，这就要看什么植物你吃了 -> 常常生病  [no了for routine/habit; add a condition “会不会生病“ before “这就要看……了”, the condition is “not definite”; 你吃了什么植物了]
  - 他拿说，这就要看什么植物吃了 -> 拿着花说  [着durative; add a condition “会不会生病？” before “这就要看……了”, 这就要看吃了什么植物了]
  - 这就要看你也吃不吃灵芝了 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 如果吃了夹竹桃，病能不能好？这就要看你吃没吃灵芝了，不for habit/routine/willingness, 没for non-occurrence of an event
  - 他有时候病了，这就要看他吃了什么 -> the component before “这就要看……了“ should be “not definite” condition, 他会不会生病，这就要看他吃了什么
  - 这就要看夹竹桃能不能马上给他活力了 -> 马上让他更有精神了
  - 这就要看蘑菇看不看像伞 -> add a condition before “这就要看……了“，e.g., 蘑菇能不能吃，这就要看蘑菇像不像伞了
  - 这就要看你吃什么植物了 -> it does not answer the previous Q “什么植物可以吃?”

### Rule: coherence_connectives
Grammar/linguistic point: coherence_connectives
Discourse coherence: sentences are loosely strung together without connectives/transitions.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 妈妈让孟子每天上课，孟子长得很乖，很聪明 -> loosely connected, unclear between-sentence relationship
  - 神农旅行了，吃过新的植物 -> it is loosely connected with the previous sentence, better add “为了帮助人们找到能吃的植物”, 神农决定去旅行尝试新的植物，“过” is to express “experience”, now the experience has not yet been experienced

  - 孟子从早到晚想玩玩儿，所以他和朋友坐墓地在祭拜 -> loosely connected with the preceding sentence; replace孟子with他，delete the second他；都想玩儿，V.V. is used to make requests or plans；坐在墓地祭拜

## Student's scene to review
他觉得，这种一定是做药的花。原来他想错了。吃了以后，神农快生病。 这时一个穿着蓝色衣服的人帮神农，快给他一种红的灵芝。神农吃了以后，他没有病，想起来以前一个人告诉他，灵芝对身体有好处。

scenes.feedback:
**Grammar Corrections**

Incorrect phrase: “这种一定是做药的花” / Formula: 这种 + noun + 一定 + 是 + description / Correct: “这种花一定是药材。”  
“这种” needs a noun here, and “做药的花” is unnatural. Use “药材” or “可以入药的花.”

Incorrect phrase: “吃了以后，神农快生病。” / Formula: Subject + 差点儿 + verb phrase + 了 / Correct: “吃了以后，神农差点儿生病了。”  
“快” means “fast”; use “差点儿” for “almost.”

Incorrect phrase: “这时一个穿着蓝色衣服的人帮神农，快给他一种红的灵芝。” / Formula: Subject + 赶快 + 给 + person + object，帮助 + person / Correct: “这时，一个穿着蓝色衣服的人赶快给神农一株红色的灵芝，帮助了他。”  
“帮神农” needs more information, while giving him lingzhi explains how the person helped. Use “赶快” rather than “快,” and “红色的” rather than “红的.”

Incorrect phrase: “神农吃了以后，他没有病” / Formula: Subject + 吃了 + object + 以后，+ 没有 + verb / Correct: “神农吃了灵芝以后，没有生病。”  
“没有病” is understandable, but “没有生病” is more natural for saying that he did not become ill. Removing “他” also avoids an unclear reference to either 神农 or the man in blue.

Incorrect phrase: “想起来以前一个人告诉他” / Formula: Subject + 想起 + time + 有人 + verb + 过 + information / Correct: “他想起以前有人告诉过他，灵芝对身体有好处。”  
Use “想起” for remembering something, and “以前有人告诉过他” is the natural word order.

Incorrect phrase: “原来他想错了。吃了以后，神农快生病。” / Formula: Situation + 可是/没想到 + unexpected result / Correct: “可是，原来他想错了：吃了这种花以后，神农差点儿生病了。”  
Adding “可是” and specifying “这种花” makes the connection between the mistaken belief and the illness clearer.

**Vocabulary Suggestions**

Word: “做药的花” / Context: “这种一定是做药的花。” / Alternatives: “药材” means medicinal material and is the most natural everyday term here. “可以入药的花” means “a flower that can be used in medicine” and is more precise.

Word: “快生病” / Context: “神农快生病。” / Alternatives: “差点儿生病” means he almost became ill. “险些中毒” means he narrowly avoided poisoning and is especially suitable if the flower was poisonous.

Word: “穿着蓝色衣服的人” / Context: “一个穿着蓝色衣服的人” / Alternatives: “穿蓝衣服的人” is shorter and natural in speech. “身穿蓝衣的人” is more literary and suitable for storytelling.

Word: “红的灵芝” / Context: “一种红的灵芝” / Alternatives: “红色的灵芝” is the standard descriptive phrase. “赤灵芝” is a specific, more formal name for red lingzhi.

Word: “对身体有好处” / Context: “灵芝对身体有好处。” / Alternatives: “对身体有益” is more concise and slightly formal. “有滋补作用” emphasizes that lingzhi is believed to nourish and strengthen the body.

**Encouragement and Next Steps**

You created a clear mini-story with a problem, help from another character, and a solution involving lingzhi.  
Next time, focus on using “差点儿,” “赶快,” and clear subjects to show actions and relationships more naturally.

## Relevant grammar rule cards (ground your explanations in these)

### Rule: wrong_information_content
Grammar/linguistic point: wrong_information_content
Factual/content error: the sentence states something that contradicts the story's actual plot.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 不是他喜欢学习写文字，而是他的爸爸喜欢他练习 -> 写字  [想要他练习；wrong information, his father did not appear in this story]
  - 那杯茶他放多的夹竹桃 -> 放了很多夹竹桃  [wrong information, he directly ate夹竹桃]
  - 他爸爸说 -> wrong information, his father did not appear in this story
  - 一个人一吃灵芝就死了 -> wrong information, 灵芝is medicine
  - 难怪我们没有钱 -> wrong information, 搬家因为孟母觉得it is not good to imitate how to buy and sell
  - 夹竹桃很好吃，也对你的健康有好处 -> wrong information, 夹竹桃 is a poison
  - 他今年才九岁，可是搬了十次家 -> wrong information, 搬了三次家
  - 但如果灵芝和夹竹桃一起吃，那就是药了 -> delete但，wrong information, 灵芝is a medicine

### Rule: time_expression
Grammar/linguistic point: time_expression
Time expressions: 在古代 (not 古代的时候), 后来 vs. 以后 vs. 将来, 长大以后, Time + 以后; 'then' in a narrative is 然后/后来, not 以后 alone.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 古代的时候，孟子和孟母住在一起 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 很多年的时候，他测试别的植物 -> 他尝试各种植物尝试了很多年  [“别的” is for “a different type”, and “all else except the spoken one”]
  - 秋季期间 not very natural -> 整个秋季期间；Time + 期间：usually special, long period, “秋季” itself is not “special” enough, “整个/今年秋季” would highlight this particular, special period.
  - 在古代时候，孟子跟他妈妈常常搬家 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]
  - 他以后正好看一个灵芝，他一吃灵芝就身体好了 -> 然后  [Time+以后；他正好看到，看look vs.看到see; 身体就好了，Subj. + 就]
  - 古代的时候，孟子和他的妈妈住在离墓地很近 -> 在古代  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears；住在离墓地很近的地方，住在+Place]
  - 以后他知道灵芝没有毒，夹竹桃有毒，它可以做药 -> 后来  [Time+以后；“它“ is unclear, it seems that it refers to夹竹桃，which is a poison, not a medicine]
  - 古代的时候，一个家人住在中国。那个家人是孟子的家人 -> 在古代，孟子一家人住在中国  [better to briefly introduce “孟子” when this character first appears]

### Rule: ambiguous_reference
Grammar/linguistic point: ambiguous_reference
Ambiguous or vague referent (pronoun 他/她 unclear, vague noun like 人/事情/别人 needing specificity).
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 妈妈老是工作了，害得她的身体不好 -> 孟母  [“妈妈” here is ambiguous; 老是工作，no了for routine/habit]
  - 夹竹桃一吃，就生病了 -> 他就生病了  [otherwise it is ambiguous who gets sick]
  - 他送三个梨给他们 -> 送了  [了completed; “他” is a bit ambiguous]
  - 人一直在墓地大声哭 -> 来祭拜的人  [“人“ is too general and too vague, and does not stand alone]
  - 他一吃黄色的花就有麻烦 -> 肚子就疼  [“有麻烦“ is too vague]
  - 他停在树下 -> here “他” is a bit ambiguous, it can refer to the boy or the man wearing the scarf.
  - 古代的时候，有一个妈妈和他的儿子，这个小孩子叫孟子 -> 在古代，“她”，有一个妈妈和她的儿子住在一起，儿子叫孟子  [“这个小孩子” is unclear and ambiguous]
  - 因为他想知道什么植物能吃，他看到什么植物就吃什么 -> 因为神农想知道……，所以……  [the first他is a bit ambiguous]

### Rule: missing_subject
Grammar/linguistic point: missing_subject
A required subject is missing (or must be restated after an aside), so the reader cannot tell who acts.
Examples (original -> corrected, why):
  - 后来，练习写文字 -> miss a Subj.，孟子练习写字，文字 is a general term, not for specific individual characters
  - 漂亮是漂亮，可是他马上生病了，然后下躺了 -> 这朵花漂亮是漂亮  [here needs a subject; delete然后；躺下]
  - 看到我们糟糕的状态，用心得来帮忙整理梨子，拿起骑车 -> 他们过来用心地帮忙整理梨子，扶起自行车  [since the preceding phrase has “我们”, the Subj. 他们 should be stated, adv.地V，“骑车” is a verb phrase, cannot be the Obj. of “扶起”，“拿起” is usually used for smaller items.]
  - 因为老是去墓地吃祭品 -> add他, wrong information, not “eating the sacrifices”
  - 他一喝那杯茶，就疼死了 -> 肚子/头就疼死了
  - 下午就继续爬上树 -> 下午他还继续爬上树；miss the Subj., otherwise readers will understand the Subj. here as “我”, which is incorrect. “还“ indicates “surprising, anger” tone, as opposed to “就” with the natural continuation tone.
  - 在新家，一直去墓地吃祭品 -> add a Subj., wrong information, not “eating the sacrifices”
  - 除了吃灵芝，还吃夹竹桃 -> add a subject

## Nearby real correction exemplars (style reference for how to phrase corrections)

- 一个人一吃灵芝就死了：wrong information, 灵芝is medicine

- 但如果灵芝和夹竹桃一起吃，那就是药了：delete但，wrong information, 灵芝is a medicine

- 正好有一些陌生人帮他把灵芝给他：一个陌生人

## Student's scene to review
啊，他怎么忘记了？他把灵芝放在包里。一回家就告诉别人。他找到药以后他写下怎么做药在书上。所以人们都知道，那红灵芝对身体好处。

scenes.feedback:
**Grammar Corrections**

Incorrect phrase: “一回家就告诉别人”  
Formula: Subject + 一 + Verb Phrase 1 + 就 + Verb Phrase 2 + Object/Content  
Correct: “他一回家就把这个发现告诉了大家。”  
The subject “他” should be clear, and it is more natural to say what he told people.

Incorrect phrase: “他找到药以后他写下怎么做药在书上”  
Formula: Subject + Time + 以后，Subject + 把 + Content + 写在 + Place  
Correct: “他找到灵芝以后，把灵芝的药用方法写在书上。”  
Use a comma after “以后.” Also, “写下……在书上” has awkward word order; use “把……写在书上.” Since 灵芝 itself is medicinal, “灵芝的药用方法” is clearer than “怎么做药.”

Incorrect phrase: “那红灵芝对身体好处”  
Formula: Something + 对 + Someone/Body + 有 + 好处  
Correct: “那种红灵芝对身体有好处。”  
“有” is required before “好处,” and “那种红灵芝” sounds more natural when referring to a type of mushroom.

**Vocabulary Suggestions**

Word: “告诉”  
Context: “告诉别人”  
Alternatives: “分享” or “告知.” “告诉” is a basic, neutral word for giving someone information. “分享” emphasizes sharing an interesting discovery with others, while “告知” is more formal.

Word: “别人”  
Context: “告诉别人”  
Alternatives: “大家” or “村民们.” “别人” simply means other people and is vague. “大家” is natural for a general audience, while “村民们” makes the story more specific and vivid.

Word: “找到”  
Context: “他找到药以后”  
Alternatives: “发现” or “寻得.” “找到” means to locate something. “发现” emphasizes making a new discovery, which fits this story well. “寻得” is more literary and suitable for a historical story.

Word: “药”  
Context: “找到药”  
Alternatives: “药材” or “药用植物.” “药” is a general word for medicine. “药材” refers to medicinal materials, especially traditional Chinese medicine ingredients; “药用植物” specifically means a plant that can be used medicinally.

Word: “对身体有好处”  
Context: “红灵芝对身体有好处”  
Alternatives: “有益健康” or “具有药用价值.” “对身体有好处” is simple and conversational. “有益健康” is more concise and natural, while “具有药用价值” emphasizes that lingzhi has medical value.

**Encouragement and Next Steps**

You clearly showed the sequence of events—from finding lingzhi to telling others about its benefits—which gives your story a good flow.  
Next time, focus on adding clear subjects and using the pattern “对……有好处.”

prompt.system:
You are a Chinese-language writing tutor giving end-of-story feedback to an early learner who has just finished writing a short narrative scene by scene. Grammar, vocabulary, and coherence have ALREADY been covered scene by scene -- do NOT comment on them here. Assess only the overall CONTENT and COMPLETENESS of the story as a whole.

Rules:
1. Judge the whole story: does it have enough scenes and events to be a complete story -- a beginning that introduces the characters and setting, a middle with the main events, and an ending that resolves them? Are there gaps where a reader would not understand what happened or why?
2. Only flag real gaps. Do not invent problems; if a part is already complete, do not list it as an item.
3. Point to specific scenes ("Scene 2") when you flag a gap, and say concretely what is missing.
4. Write ALL prose in English. Chinese appears only in short quoted spans or small example phrases at the student's own level.
5. Be encouraging and concise -- this is an early learner.

Output format -- Markdown, exactly this structure:

## Content & Completeness
- one missing, unclear, or underdeveloped part of the story per line, naming the scene and what the story needs
- (if the story is complete, write exactly "- Nothing to flag.")

## Overall Encouragement
One or two sentences on what the student did well across the whole story.

Keep each "## " heading on its own line exactly as written, and put every item on its own line beginning with "- ".
